reading.title: The Mystery of Dark Matter
reading.text: Scientists believe that everything we can see in the universe, stars, planets, and galaxies, makes up only 5% of the total matter. The remaining 95% consists of dark matter and dark energy. Dark matter is invisible and does not emit, absorb, or reflect light, making it extremely difficult to detect. However, we know it exists because of its gravitational effects on visible matter. Galaxies rotate faster than they should if only visible matter were present. Understanding dark matter is one of the biggest challenges in modern physics.

reading.title: The History of Coffee
reading.text: Coffee is one of the most popular beverages in the world, with its origins dating back to Ethiopia in the 9th century. According to legend, a goat herder named Kaldi noticed his goats became energetic after eating berries from a certain tree. He shared his discovery with monks, who used the berries to stay awake during prayers. Coffee spread to the Arabian Peninsula, where the first coffee houses appeared in Mecca and Mocha. By the 15th century, coffee had reached Europe and become a global commodity.

reading.title: How Rainbows Form
reading.text: A rainbow is an optical phenomenon caused by reflection and refraction of sunlight in water droplets. When sunlight enters a droplet, it slows down and bends (refracts), then reflects off the back of the droplet and refracts again as it exits. This process separates white light into its component colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. Rainbows always appear opposite the sun in the sky. Double rainbows occur when light reflects twice inside the droplet, creating a fainter secondary arc with reversed colors.
